items.title: Eddie Palmieri — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Billy Taylor had a thing on that, an exposé on that.

ctx.x: The cabaret card. It’s a racial situation there, because there was too many blacks and Hispanics working downtown. As long as you stayed uptown, Minton’s the jazz room, you were fine. You come down to Broadway...you know, downtown... So we had to go to the police department. Billy Taylor had a thing on that, an exposé on that. You had to get your fingerprints and a card. Without the card, you couldn’t play any place they served liquor, so you’re out of business. It happened to all the top jazz players that got…

Because I knew I wasn’t going to miss. I knew it intuitively, like I said, but as I studied with Bob, then I learned it scientifically, again with that tension-and-resistance thing. “Oh, now we got it!” You know what I mean?
